decisions.reason: It fits the firm's core industrial door range and remained marketed after launch, so from a behavioral-theory view it likely met at least acceptable aspirations and is worth retaining unless portfolio overlap triggers rationalization.

As an insulated glazed industrial door, it matches the firm's compliance- and performance-oriented strategy, and a large firm with some slack would usually keep such a core-adjacent product once early results appear satisfactory.

Its continued dedicated presentation after launch suggests results were not below aspiration, so management would most likely keep it, though some risk remains if similar glazed door variants are consolidated.
